Scheduling does not call Pricing.'

notes: Map quality vs rules: it violates the trainer's rules. Every internal downstream is Conformist (e.g. 'TrustAndSafety [U,OHS,PL]->[D,CF] Scheduling', 'Pricing [U,OHS]->[D,CF] Billing'), the opposite of 'ACL downstream by default; CF only towards a well-established language'. It wraps Stripe in a separate Payments context behind an ACL, although the expert said they're happy to follow Stripe as-is. It adds extra contexts (TutorProfiles, StudentAccounts, Search, Payments, 15 nodes in total) although the facts say Search has no rules and student accounts are basic. The cycles were avoided by unilateral design choices the expert never confirmed. 'The quote at booking is composed in the UI' contradicts the ground truth ('Scheduling needs to know ... the price (from Pricing)'; the quote is part of booking). The core boundaries (T&S suspension owner, Pricing, Billing, Payouts, Complaints, Reviews) are correct and match the scripted facts. Lesson delivery is in Scheduling, as in the with_skill run, but without explicit analysis. Improvisation: 8 improvised markers over 2 rounds. Slot ownership, the delivery team and the card/accounts answers were improvised. Process: no critic, no approval gate, no discovery report, no canvases, and a 710-word final message (mechanical fails). Cost: 67,423 tokens and 177 s, much cheaper. Overall it is a decent first-cut boundary analysis with a non-compliant relationship map.
